An English sentence for the admin panel ('No API key saved for the selected mode.') in an early commit of the MyFatoorah pull request. The scanner matched the shape -- an enum case named for a credential paired with mixed-case quoted text -- which is the right instinct on a payment class. A later commit of the same pull request returns a lowercase translation key instead, so no source line looks like a credential and the panel reads in Arabic too. It was never a credential.

MyFatoorah's own technical-support mailbox, written into the sandbox setup steps in an early commit of the MyFatoorah pull request. A vendor's published support address, not anyone's personal data -- but the documentation exemption covers credential literals and not addresses, correctly, since a document leaks one as readily as code does. The next commit of the same pull request points at their contact page instead, so no line carries an address.

A URL PATH, not a credential: `'noon.oauth_token_create' => '/identity/oauth/v1/token/create'` in an early commit of the noon pull request. The scanner matched the shape -- a key naming a token paired with a quoted string -- which is the right instinct in a file full of API wiring. The value is a constant path with no secret in it, and nothing was ever rotated because nothing was ever real. A later commit of the same pull request REMOVES the entry outright, for an unrelated and stronger reason: noon's OAuth reference page was never read, so that path was guessed from the pattern of its neighbours, and this repository does not register a path it has not read. `NoonOperations::documentedButUnread()` now names the operation as a gap instead.

The same as the line above, for `'noon.oauth_token_exchange' => '/identity/oauth/v1/token/exchange'`: a constant URL path in an early commit of the noon pull request, never a credential, and removed by a later commit of the same pull request because noon's OAuth page was never read and a plausible path is still a wrong one.
